quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on a film of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes extra slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: If worried, nervous, angry, or crying, a driver:

options.text: Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more in touch with their senses.
Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to vent while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind is focused on something else instead of the road. Calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: You are involved in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured away from the scene immediately.
Always leave the injured where they are.
Not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you that a lane is ending. Get ready to let other traffic merge safely.

questions.question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, it is a good idea to:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours during a long trip to take a short break. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and nap, or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction. Your headlights:

options.text: Should be on their high beam setting.
Should be on their low beam setting.
Should be off. Use your parking lights.
May be on either their high or low beam setting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be on their low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Switch to low beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night. This keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: Which of the following substances may impair your ability to drive safely and may result in an arrest for driving under the influence (DUI)?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other liquor
Illegal drugs and prescription medicines
Inhalants, such as glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and are approaching a heavy truck from the rear. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On a hill with poor visibility, it is against the law to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes are becoming one lane ahead. You need to merge into a single lane.

questions.question: What do highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows painted in the lanes show drivers which lanes to use. They tell you whether to go straight or turn.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the chance of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, what must a driver do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right of way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must try to prevent hitting any pedestrian, no matter what. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, look to make sure it is safe, and then go.

questions.question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights
High beam headlights
Parking lights
No lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right
Double curve
Winding road
Pavement ends

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has many turns and curves.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view
When exiting an expressway
When following a motorcycle
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway
Accelerating quickly
Slowing down gradually
Braking hard

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually
questions.explanation: Every quick stop wastes fuel because you must accelerate again. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking, you use less gas.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the driver's way
Stare at the driver as they pass
Speed up as they pass you
Block the passing lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the driver's way
questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up or blocking the lane will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. If you see yellow, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, a driver should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to drivers already on the interstate. Merge safely into traffic when you have space.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn in curves. Slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: What does an orange sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash lights and sound your horn to alert drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass, the risk of a collision increases. If you drive faster than others, you must keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, stay within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
There is a higher chance of seeing pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during posted times. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and how much oncoming traffic there is.

questions.question: What can state and local authorities do about speed limits?

options.text: Must post the same speed limit for all similar roads.
Can change speed limits in specific areas by posting signs.
Cannot post different speed limits.
Must never post a speed limit lower than 35 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change speed limits in specific areas by posting signs.
questions.explanation: State and local authorities can change speed limits in specific areas by posting new signs. Follow the posted speed limit when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed if they break traffic laws.

questions.question: When are roads most slick?

options.text: When it just starts to rain
When the temperature is below freezing
Both of the above
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: Roads are slick when rain first starts because water mixes with oil on the road, making it greasy. Roads are also slick when moisture freezes in cold temperatures, creating ice.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before red.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Slow down to stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What is true about larger vehicles?

options.text: They have larger blind spots.
They have smaller blind spots.
They have no blind spots.
They have the same blind spots as small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles like trucks and SUVs have bigger blind spots. There are areas behind and beside them that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: Which of these does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, blurs your vision, damages your judgment of speed and distance, and reduces your ability to handle headlight glare. It does not help you calm down or concentrate better.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a person is ahead controlling traffic in a construction zone.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will make a sharp turn to the right and then to the left.
